title: Inline
summary: A horizontal row that wraps onto new rows when its children do not fit is the standard FlowRow, with spacing from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For rows of buttons, tags, badges or metadata that must not overflow a narrow screen or a large font size.
whenNotToUse: For a row that must stay on one line use a Row (with weights, or horizontalScroll for overflow). For a grid of equal tiles use LazyVerticalGrid (see grid).
api: @Composable inline fun FlowRow(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = Arrangement.Top, itemVerticalAlignment: Alignment.Vertical = Alignment.Top, maxItemsInEachRow: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, content: @Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)
fun Arrangement.spacedBy(space: Dp, alignment: Alignment.Horizontal): Arrangement.Horizontal
appearance: No appearance of its own: the children are Monarch components; the gaps are steps of the space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Inline is a flex row with wrap, a gap, align and justify. On Android the gap is horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(space) for the gap between items and verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(space) for the gap between rows; align is itemVerticalAlignment; justify is the alignment argument of spacedBy (Alignment.CenterHorizontally, Alignment.End). The web's wrap={false} is a Row. FlowRow mirrors in a right-to-left layout. iOS has no wrapping stack and builds MonarchFlowLayout; Android uses the platform FlowRow and ships nothing.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads the children in order, row by row, starting at the start edge.
At font scale 2.0 children wrap onto more rows instead of being cut.
edgeCases: A child wider than the row takes a row of its own and is measured at the full width.
FlowRow is experimental in some Compose versions; Monarch's examples opt in to ExperimentalLayoutApi.
